records.claim: When taken by mouth or through an IV, only a small amount of clindamycin passes into breast milk. Babies sometimes receive clindamycin directly to treat infections, so a nursing infant would get much less from breast milk than from a direct dose. Because the amount of clindamycin in breast milk is low, side effects are unlikely for most babies. Watch the baby for any stomach issues, like diarrhea or diaper rash, and contact their healthcare provider if you notice anything. Very little clindamycin applied to the skin or used vaginally is absorbed into the body, so it is unlikely to reach breast milk in amounts that could affect a nursing baby.
